cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, with a message for the Israelites. It's about one certain kind of sin, and what to do about it. Friend, I love a good system, and this is a WHOLE system.

cards.question: The LORD's message is about someone who sins against His commandments in what way?

cards.text: First on the list is the anointed priest. And friend, when HE sins, it doesn't stay with him.

cards.question: When the anointed priest sins, who does it bring guilt on?

cards.text: He brings the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering, lays his hand on its head and slaughters it before the LORD. He takes some of its blood into the Tent of Meeting, sprinkles it seven times before the LORD in front of the veil, and puts some on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. The rest of the blood is poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, and all the fat is burned on that altar. Everything else, from the hide to the head, is burned on a wood fire outside the camp, at a ceremonially clean place on the ash heap.
Now zoom out: what if the WHOLE congregation of Israel strays unintentionally, and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly? That's a group chat where EVERYBODY missed the same message.

cards.question: When does the whole assembly bring its sin offering?

answers.text: When they become aware of the sin
On the next day of rest
At the end of the year

cards.question: The assembly brings a young bull before the Tent of Meeting. Who lays their hands on its head before it's slaughtered?

cards.text: Then the anointed priest runs the same steps: blood into the Tent, seven sprinkles in front of the veil, blood on the horns, the rest at the base, fat on the altar. Same steps, and I respect it, because I've stamped the same cookie ten THOUSAND times and I still check the dough.

cards.question: For the whole assembly's sin offering, the elders of the congregation make atonement on their behalf.
For the whole assembly, the priest makes atonement on their behalf, and they will be ___.

cards.text: Then that bull goes outside the camp and gets burned, just like the first one. Next case: a leader sins unintentionally.

cards.question: A leader who sins unintentionally against the LORD's commandments still incurs guilt.

cards.text: Being in charge doesn't come with an undo button, friend. Once he becomes aware of it, he brings an unblemished male goat, lays his hand on its head and slaughters it where the burnt offering is slaughtered. The priest puts some of its blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, pours out the rest at its base, and burns all the fat on the altar. That's how the priest makes atonement for the leader's sin, and he will be forgiven.

Now one of the common people sins unintentionally and incurs guilt. Finally, somebody regular like ME, friend: no title, no anointing, just a mustache and a dream! Once he becomes aware of it, he brings an unblemished female goat, lays his hand on its head and slaughters it at the place of the burnt offering. The priest puts some of its blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pours out the rest at its base.

cards.question: The priest removes all the fat from the common person's goat and burns it on the altar. He burns it as what?

answers.text: A pleasing aroma to the LORD
A warning to the whole camp

cards.question: Instead of a goat, the common person may bring an unblemished female lamb. With the lamb, just like with the goat, the priest makes atonement for him and he will be forgiven.

cards.text: Then the LORD gets specific: someone hears a public charge about something he witnessed, and he doesn't testify, so he bears the iniquity. That's the coworker who saw EXACTLY who took the parking spot and suddenly can't remember a thing.

cards.question: If someone touches something unclean, like the carcass of an unclean animal, without knowing it, he is still unclean and guilty.

cards.text: Same with touching human uncleanness without knowing it. Once he realizes it, he is guilty.

cards.question: If someone swears an oath without thinking, he isn't guilty as long as the oath was to do something good.
Whether he stayed silent as a witness, touched something unclean or swore an oath without thinking, a person who incurs guilt in one of these ways must ___ the sin he has committed.

cards.text: Then he brings a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering, and the priest makes atonement for him. But what if a lamb costs more than he's got?

cards.question: If a person can't afford a lamb, he has to wait until he can afford one before he brings his sin offering.

cards.text: Instead, he may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons. The priest offers the first bird as the sin offering and prepares the second as a burnt offering, and the man will be forgiven. Same forgiveness, SMALLER wallet!

And if he can't afford two birds either, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. A grain offering of fine flour gets olive oil and frankincense (Leviticus 2:1), but this flour gets neither.

cards.question: Why does the flour for this sin offering get no olive oil and no frankincense?

answers.text: Because it is a sin offering
Because the oil is for the lamps

cards.question: The priest burns a handful of the flour on the altar as a memorial portion. Flour is the last option, for someone who can't afford even two birds. Which of the sins the LORD listed can the priest make atonement for with it?

cards.text: He will be forgiven, and the rest of the flour belongs to the priest, like the grain offering. Stick around, friend, because this teaching on the offerings isn't finished yet.
